examples.name: Supervisor loop with specialist roles and typed handoffs
examples.mechanism: Conductor owns episode lifecycle, budgets and arbitration but executes no tool. Plan nodes become typed handoffs claimed by one specialist with a lease; transient refusals retry once, terminal refusals stop the episode, payload shapes are validated, and the verdict is assembled from gate report + blind critique.

examples.name: Episode ledger, hash chain, write path and retrieval
examples.mechanism: Append-only hash-chained event log (seq, prev_hash, kind, payload); transactional close that validates the chain, closes the episode and indexes a tsvector case; bounded retrieval with hard filters, lexical rank, rerank and a retrieval receipt. Empty retrieval is recorded honestly.

examples.name: Visual critic with rendered evidence, diagnostics and rubric
examples.mechanism: Blind schema-constrained critic: brief + rubric + rendered images only; every dimension cites an existing crop region and an observation; diagnostics are stored but never sent or allowed to set the verdict; confidence is model-reported, grounding-capped and never presented as accuracy; low confidence routes to a human.
inputs: CritiqueInput {artifact hash, brief, renders[], metrics, rubric[]}
outputs: CritiqueReport {dimensions, defects, reported/effective confidence, unseen, verdict, image hashes, raw hash}

failurePath.failure: malformed JSON / missing evidence / bad crop

examples.name: Skill promotion and rollback: candidate to active, evidence, version pin
examples.mechanism: Procedural memory changes only through a statistical reversible gate: ≥3 independent episodes with distinct inputs, passing golden regression, named human sign-off; transactional supersede + insert with exactly one active version; rollback flips the pointer to a prior version and records the reason; pins bind skill version to app version and catalogue hash.
verified: [R] Promotion policy and pointer-flip rollback from 04 §8.4–8.5 and the installed memory-ledger reference
[V] No skill/ledger tables exist in the deployed pod DB (04 §2.4; 01 §11)
[V] Sketch compiled and 5/5 Example-5 checks passed in the scratch harness
proposed: [I] Partial unique index enforcing one active version
[I] Evidence independence definition (distinct episodes and inputs)
unverified: SQL and concurrency behaviour on PostgreSQL 16

examples.name: RL-shaped eval loop with verifiable gates and anti-reward-hacking
examples.mechanism: Evaluate retrieval + active skills as policy arms against a public/private golden set. Reward is a hard conjunction of verified properties, never a scalar proxy. Detectors cover private leakage, baseline-arm contamination, gate authorship, brief drift, input override, shortcuts, cost anomaly, skipped critic and threshold hugging. Lift is tested with Wilson/Newcombe intervals; null result is hold.
inputs: GoldenTask[] (public/private, input hash, brief hash, floors, gates)
outputs: EvalReport {baseline, memory, lift, lift_ci, regressions, flags, verdict}

failurePath.behavior: honest null result; memory arm off by default

verified: [R] Golden split, metrics, A/B protocol, anti-hack checks and regression gates from 04 §9
